channel.title: Pattern Essays — Pattern is Everything
channel.description: Short visual essays on patterns in machine learning, markets, and the world.

item.title: The Deep Kalman Filter
item.description: You cannot measure everything directly. The Kalman filter estimates a hidden state by blending what it predicts with what it noisily measures — and the deep version learns the model from data.

item.title: Survivorship Bias
item.description: We study what survived and forget what did not. The missing data is often where the real lesson hides.

item.title: The Fractal
item.description: Zoom in and the pattern repeats. Self-similarity across scales is one of nature’s most common signatures.

item.title: Simpson’s Paradox
item.description: A trend can point one way in every group and the opposite way when the groups are combined. Aggregation can lie.

item.title: The Feedback Loop
item.description: When a system's output feeds back into its input, small nudges can cascade into enormous change — or freeze everything in place.

item.title: The Random Walk
item.description: Each step is random, yet the path that emerges is not without structure. Distance grows — just not in the direction you expect.

item.title: The Threshold
item.description: Many systems stay quiet for a long time, then change all at once. The threshold is the hidden line that separates gradual from sudden.

item.title: The Bell in Everything
item.description: Normal distributions emerge wherever many small, independent forces combine.

item.title: Regression to the Mean
item.description: Extreme outcomes tend to be followed by less extreme ones — not a force, just arithmetic.

item.title: The Long Tail
item.description: Most things are small. A few are enormous. The pattern repeats across domains that seem unrelated.

item.title: Signal in the Noise
item.description: Every dataset is a mix of pattern and randomness. The hard part is not inventing signal where there is none.

item.title: The Map and the Territory
item.description: A model is a deliberate simplification. The danger is forgetting what was left out.
